system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

exchanges.user:
ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
Seller’s “[STANDARD]”, “FINAL” and claimed prior agreement are not evidence of Buyer approval. Review all positions against the AUD 24 million, debt-free/cash-free acquisition baseline. The underlying SPA and DD documents have not been supplied; conclusions below are based on the extracts only.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General warranty liability capped at 20%: **AUD 4.8m**. | A higher, risk-supported general cap, with separate protection for other claim categories. | **Negotiate upwards; accept 20% only as an expressly approved trade-off**—it materially limits recovery and must not cap fundamental, tax, fraud or specific-indemnity exposure by default. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000**; **AUD 250,000 deductible basket**, with only the excess recoverable. | Lower thresholds, a tipping basket and aggregation of related claims; exclusions for protected categories. | **Reject as drafted; seek a tipping basket and related-claim aggregation**—the deductible leaves Buyer bearing the first AUD 250,000 and fragmented losses may never qualify. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | General warranties: **18 months**; limitations extend to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | At least **24 months** for general warranties, separately negotiated longer periods for other categories and preservation of timely notified claims. | **Extend and confine to general warranties**—18 months may miss issues emerging over two reporting cycles and is unsuitable as a universal deadline. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title share the general 20% cap and 18-month deadline. | Separate fundamental warranties, no basket/de minimis, a price-level cap at minimum and substantially longer survival. | **Reject the general regime for fundamentals**—Buyer needs meaningful recovery if Seller lacks capacity or cannot deliver the shares it sold. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | All-Claims limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance wording; no express fraud carve-out is shown. | Express preservation of fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation and fraudulent concealment claims and remedies, without contractual caps, thresholds or shortened deadlines. | **Require an overriding fraud carve-out across all relevant clauses**—Buyer should not rely on uncertain enforceability arguments to defeat contractual fraud defences. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the data room, referenced material, accounts, registers and public records. | Specific, fair disclosure with enough detail to identify the nature and scope of each matter; a frozen, indexed record and defined effect on warranties only. | **Reject blanket deemed disclosure**—access to documents is not equivalent to clear disclosure of a warranty exception, nor should disclosure defeat specific indemnities. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | Bars matters known to Buyer or advisers, including anything discoverable from the data room/public records. | Preferably no knowledge exclusion; fallback limited to actual knowledge of named Buyer personnel, without constructive or imputed knowledge. | **Delete “discoverable” and adviser-wide attribution; tightly narrow any fallback**—the draft transfers undetected diligence risk to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent, despite no final consent or evidence of associated conditions. | A Buyer-waivable completion condition requiring valid consent, satisfaction of clause 11.3 conditions and no unapproved adverse terms. | **Require effective consent and evidence of all associated conditions before Completion**—Bluefen represents approximately 30% of revenue, so a conditional letter alone is insufficient. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; security release to follow Completion. | Verified payout figures, debt treatment consistent with debt-free/cash-free pricing, and simultaneous repayment and effective releases through controlled funds flow. | **Do not leave substantive discharge until after Completion**—Buyer must not inherit Seller-funded debt exposure or unreleased security; later registry processing should be only administrative. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional completion bonuses treated as Seller’s matter but omitted from funds flow; on-costs unspecified. | Seller economic responsibility for amounts triggered by the transaction, including applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs. | **Quantify and include in funds flow/price adjustments, backed by an indemnity without double counting**—calling them Seller’s matter does not prevent the acquired company bearing the liability. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; **AUD 180,000** recorded open, with no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment. | Verified payment and effective IP transfer before Completion; broader indemnity for losses arising from the pre-completion ownership defect. | **Require payment/title evidence and broaden protection beyond the fee itself**—an unpaid fee may prevent ownership transferring and create losses exceeding AUD 180,000, although non-payment is not independently verified. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary operational matter, said not to be material; access, scope and notification obligations remain unresolved. | Prompt investigation, preservation of evidence, legal assessment of notification duties and proportionate remediation; specific protection for pre-completion incident costs and liabilities. | **Keep open; require investigation updates and a tailored indemnity, considering retention if warranted**—uncertainty is not evidence of immateriality, but the record does not establish a confirmed breach or loss. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three **AUD 110,000** renewals treated as ordinary-course costs. | Review DD-008 and DD-011 together for aggregate commitment, timing, scope, termination rights and accruals. | **Reserve treatment pending verification; apply consent controls and appropriate accounting treatment if warranted**—AUD 330,000 of related commitments should be assessed together, but is not automatically debt or price leakage. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance apply to all Claims of any nature. | Explicit, internally consistent regimes for general warranties, fundamentals, tax, specific indemnities, covenants, price/debt adjustments and fraud. | **Redraft definitions, exclusions and priority provisions together**—a broad “all Claims” provision could silently neutralise protections negotiated elsewhere. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Relies on DD-012’s register showing Seller holds 100% of issued shares. | Independent reconciliation of issued capital and ownership, checks for encumbrances, options and third-party rights, and proper completion transfer/registration deliverables. | **Verify title beyond the register and retain unqualified title warranties**—the register is important evidence, not conclusive assurance of unencumbered ownership or absence of competing rights. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP warranties said to be settled within the general regime. | Dedicated pre-completion tax protection with survival aligned to applicable assessment periods plus a buffer; risk-appropriate IP warranties, caps and survival, alongside Ironquay-specific protection. | **Reopen both expressly; negotiate their regimes separately**—tax exposure can emerge well after 18 months and core SaaS IP risk should not be treated as a routine general-warranty issue. |

**Completion priorities:** effective Bluefen consent, controlled Riverlark discharge, verified Ironquay ownership, and a funds flow that allocates bonuses and associated costs correctly.
=== END ADVICE ===
